title: Predict how far a gradient travels
brief: Compute the spectral radius, use it to predict how large a gradient is after many steps, and ask how many steps it takes to fall below a threshold. Then compare the prediction with the gradient your own backward pass measures.
hints: np.linalg.eigvals returns complex numbers for many real matrices. Take np.abs of them before np.max.
gradient_scale_over_time is (kappa * rho) ** T, with rho from your spectral_radius.

steps_until_below: solve rate ** T < threshold. Taking logs flips the inequality because log(rate) is negative, so T > log(threshold) / log(rate), and the answer is the next whole number above that. Return None when the rate is 1 or more.
